reasoning: The spec demands coupling_ratio=0.9439 AND a <=40x4.5 um footprint simultaneously. On TFLN (core_n=2.138, clad_n=1.444, t=0.4 um) the mode is weakly confined, so the two-core supermode split is tiny even at the tightest allowed gap. At w=single_mode_width_um=1.2 and gap=min_feature_um=0.50 (the SMALLEST gap the DRC permits), solve_supermodes gives dn=0.003771 -> beat length Lpi=205.52 um. coupling_ratio=sin^2(pi*L/(2*Lpi)); reaching 0.9439 requires L/Lpi=2*asin(sqrt(0.9439))/pi=0.847767, i.e. coupling_length=174.23 um. The device length is 2*sbend_length + coupling_length, so even with sbend_length=2.0 the bbox is 178.2 um long = 4.5x the 40 um budget. The only two knobs that could shorten Lpi are barred: width is pinned to single_mode_width_um by the platform-adaptation rule, and gap is already at min_feature_um. Reducing coupling_length to fit the footprint (max ~36 um) collapses the ratio to ~0.074, far below the 0.8939 acceptance floor. Ratio and footprint are therefore mutually exclusive within the exposed tunables. Confirmed by eval: at the ratio-correct L=174.23 the metric passes (0.94387) but footprint_ok=false (bbox 178.2x4.2).

tunables.note: wg_width=single_mode_width_um and coupling_gap=min_feature_um are the platform floors; coupling_length shown is the ratio-correct value that overflows the footprint. No value of coupling_length satisfies ratio and footprint together.
